name: Question 12
worked_solution:
First, let's recall the secant-tangent identity:

$$
1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta 
$$

We rewrite the given expression using the secant-tangent identity as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{(1-{cos}^{2}⁡x)(1+{tan}^{2}⁡x)} & =\frac{1}{(1-{cos}^{2}⁡x)\cdot ({sec}^{2}⁡x)}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we recall the following identities:

$$
1-{cos}^{2}⁡x={sin}^{2}⁡x,\,\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x},\,\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x},\,\operatorname{cot}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{tan}⁡x}
$$

 

Using the above identities, we can further simplify our expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{(1-{cos}^{2}⁡x)\cdot ({sec}^{2}⁡x)} & =\frac{1}{({sin}^{2}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡x})} \\  & =\frac{1}{(\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡x}{{cos}^{2}⁡x})} \\  & =\frac{1}{{(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{{tan}^{2}⁡x} \\  & ={cot}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{1}{(1-{cos}^{2}⁡x)(1+{tan}^{2}⁡x)}={cot}^{2}⁡x.
$$

EXPLANATION

First, let's recall the secant-tangent identity:

1+tan2⁡θ=sec2⁡θ

We rewrite the given expression using the secant-tangent identity as follows:

1(1−cos2⁡x)(1+tan2⁡x)=1(1−cos2⁡x)⋅(sec2⁡x)

Next, we recall the following identities:

1−cos2⁡x=sin2⁡x,sec⁡x=1cos⁡x,tan⁡θ=sin⁡xcos⁡x,cot⁡x=1tan⁡x

Using the above identities, we can further simplify our expression as follows:

1(1−cos2⁡x)⋅(sec2⁡x)=1(sin2⁡x⋅1cos2⁡x)=1(sin2⁡xcos2⁡x)=1(sin⁡xcos⁡x)2=1tan2⁡x=cot2⁡x

Therefore, we conclude that

1(1−cos2⁡x)(1+tan2⁡x)=cot2⁡x.
